from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    fill = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # The puzzle is a regular lattice. Its horizontal and vertical rails are
    # the rows/columns mostly unlike the tile-interior background.
    line_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid)
                 if sum(v != fill for v in row) > w / 2]
    line_cols = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] != fill for r in range(h)) > h / 2]
    if len(line_rows) < 2 or len(line_cols) < 2:
        return [[fill]]

    # Ignore crossings: rail cells away from crossings reveal the divider color.
    rail_values = ([grid[r][c] for r in line_rows for c in range(w)
                    if c not in line_cols] +
                   [grid[r][c] for c in line_cols for r in range(h)
                    if r not in line_rows])
    rail = Counter(rail_values).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # A decoded pixel is colored only if the four corner crossings agree.
    decoded = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(line_rows, line_rows[1:]):
        row = []
        for c0, c1 in zip(line_cols, line_cols[1:]):
            corners = (grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1],
                       grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1])
            color = corners[0]
            row.append(color if color != rail and all(v == color for v in corners)
                       else fill)
        decoded.append(row)

    # Crop blank lattice padding around the recovered image.
    active_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(decoded)
                   if any(v != fill for v in row)]
    active_cols = [c for c in range(len(decoded[0]))
                   if any(decoded[r][c] != fill for r in range(len(decoded)))]
    if not active_rows or not active_cols:
        return [[fill]]
    return [row[active_cols[0]:active_cols[-1] + 1]
            for row in decoded[active_rows[0]:active_rows[-1] + 1]]
